Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Stimulus washout and persistence time course
ideas.description: Give a brief AP-1-inducing stimulus (e.g., TPA or EGF pulse, or a doxycycline-inducible FOS/JUN pulse), then withdraw it and track AP-1 occupancy (CUT&RUN for FOS/JUN), chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), and target transcription over days. Memory requires that AP-1 target enhancers stay open or primed after AP-1 itself has returned to baseline, so persistence beyond the signal is the key readout.

ideas.title: Re-stimulation test of primed versus naive cells
ideas.description: Compare the first and second responses to the same stimulus, measuring AP-1 target induction, Pol II loading, and enhancer accessibility. Memory predicts faster or stronger re-induction in previously stimulated cells. Pair this with CRISPR mutation of AP-1 motifs at the primed enhancers to test whether the memory depends on those specific sites.

ideas.title: Inducible degradation of AP-1 during the memory window
ideas.description: Use an auxin- or dTAG-based degron on endogenous FOS or JUN to remove AP-1 after priming but before re-stimulation. If AP-1 is the memory carrier, degradation should erase the re-induction advantage while leaving the first-response induction intact. Timing the degradation separately from the priming stimulus separates maintenance of memory from its initial establishment.

ideas.title: Coupled AP-1 and histone-mark profiling across time
ideas.description: Perform ChIP-seq or CUT&Tag for H3K27ac, H3K4me1, and H3K4me3 alongside AP-1 binding over the same time course. Memory-like behavior would show persistent deposition of activating marks at AP-1-bound enhancers after AP-1 has left them. Comparing these marks with a DNA-methylation or histone-mark-writer knockout shows whether the memory is chromatin-based or relies on AP-1 alone.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage tracing of AP-1 state heritability
ideas.description: Combine an AP-1 reporter or live-cell FOS/JUN readout with lineage barcoding so you can follow individual cells through several divisions after a pulse. Quantify how strongly AP-1 activity state in one generation predicts the state in descendants, and whether that correlation disappears when AP-1 is knocked down. Heritable, AP-1-dependent states would indicate cellular memory rather than simple reversible signaling.
